subtopicTitle: Magnetic force on charge — F = qv×B

cards.front: State the vector formula for the magnetic force $\vec{F}$ on a charge $q$ moving with velocity $\vec{v}$ in a magnetic field $\vec{B}$.
What three fundamental physical quantities determine the magnitude and direction of the magnetic force on a moving charge?
cards.back: The magnitude of the charge ($q$), its velocity ($\vec{v}$), and the magnetic field strength ($\vec{B}$). The direction is given by the cross product $\vec{v} \times \vec{B}$.

cards.front: Describe the Right-Hand Rule to find the direction of magnetic force $\vec{F}$ on a *positive* charge $q$ given $\vec{v}$ and $\vec{B}$.
cards.back: Point your right fingers in the direction of $\vec{v}$, curl them towards $\vec{B}$, and your right thumb will point in the direction of $\vec{F}$. For a negative charge, the force direction is opposite.

cards.front: List the conditions under which a charged particle moving in a magnetic field would experience *no* magnetic force.
cards.back:
The magnetic force $\vec{F} = q(\vec{v} \times \vec{B})$ is zero if:
1.  The charge $q$ is zero.
2.  The velocity $\vec{v}$ is zero (particle is stationary).
3.  The magnetic field $\vec{B}$ is zero.
4.  The velocity $\vec{v}$ is parallel or anti-parallel to the magnetic field $\vec{B}$ (i.e., $\theta = 0^\circ$ or $180^\circ$, so $\sin\theta = 0$).

cards.front: A proton ($q = +1.6 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C}$) moves at $5.0 \times 10^6 \text{ m/s}$ perpendicular to a $0.50 \text{ T}$ magnetic field. Calculate the magnitude of the magnetic force.
cards.back:
Since $\vec{v} \perp \vec{B}$, $\theta = 90^\circ$, so $\sin\theta = 1$.
$F = |q|vB\sin\theta = (1.6 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C})(5.0 \times 10^6 \text{ m/s})(0.50 \text{ T})(1)$
$F = 4.0 \times 10^{-13} \text{ N}$

cards.front: Explain why the magnetic force on a charged particle can change its direction but *not* its kinetic energy.
cards.back: The magnetic force $\vec{F}$ is always perpendicular to the velocity $\vec{v}$ of the charged particle (by definition of the cross product). Work done $W = \vec{F} \cdot \vec{d}$. Since $\vec{F} \perp \vec{v}$, and $\vec{v}$ is in the direction of infinitesimal displacement $\vec{d}$, $\vec{F}$ is also perpendicular to $\vec{d}$. Thus, the angle between $\vec{F}$ and $\vec{d}$ is $90^\circ$, so $\cos(90^\circ) = 0$, meaning $W=0$. By the Work-Energy Theorem ($W = \Delta KE$), if no work is done, the kinetic energy ($\frac{1}{2}mv^2$) cannot change.

cards.front: Derive the formula for the radius $r$ of the circular path of a charged particle ($q, m$) entering a uniform magnetic field $\vec{B}$ perpendicular to its velocity $\vec{v}$.
cards.back:
When $\vec{v} \perp \vec{B}$, the magnetic force $F_B = |q|vB$ provides the centripetal force $F_c = \frac{mv^2}{r}$.
Equating these forces:
$$|q|vB = \frac{mv^2}{r}$$
Solving for $r$:
$$r = \frac{mv^2}{|q|vB}$$
$$r = \frac{mv}{|q|B}$$
Where $m$ is the mass, $v$ is the speed, $q$ is the charge magnitude, and $B$ is the magnetic field strength.
